text: agent-generated hypothesis: A Co-Ni maraging steel (about 12-18 wt% Ni, 8-12 wt% Co) with Ti and Al additions that form a high number density of coherent Ni3(Ti,Al)/eta-type nanoprecipitates reaches about 2000 MPa yield strength after aging near 480-500 C. Co raises the martensite start temperature and promotes precipitation, and the Ti/Al content sets the precipitation strengthening.
assumption: Strength is dominated by shearable coherent nanoprecipitates at a number density of at least 1e24 per m3, with no coarsening or reverted austenite at the chosen aging time. The literature claim (rec-0005) of at least 2000 MPa transfers to the candidate composition range.

text: agent-generated hypothesis: Increasing Ti+Al total from about 1.5 to about 3 wt% in a Co-bearing Ni maraging steel raises yield strength by roughly 300-400 MPa through a higher precipitate volume fraction. Gains saturate above about 2200 MPa because of embrittlement and precipitate coarsening.
assumption: Yield strength scales roughly with the square root of precipitate volume fraction (Orowan or shearing regime), and Co content is held constant so the matrix stays fully martensitic. Ti and Al partition fully into precipitates.
